tier_reason: First-party README comparison against Boost.Geometry 1.90 R*-tree (plus nanoflann, GEOS, tidwall) with public benchmark code in the repo, but CPU model and compiler flags are not stated (only 'ASUS ROG Strix G16, Windows 11', MSVC 2026/Clang 22); the README gives rankings and a few ratios, no explicit KdBoxTree-vs-Boost ratio.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README: KdBoxTree is quickest to bulk-load, fastest at range queries on box keys and (from 10^4 elements) on point keys, fastest at nearest queries on box keys; 'Boost R-tree lags behind in query performance'; other indices build 2-4x slower and need 1.5-4x more queries to amortise their build. No single KdBoxTree-vs-Boost ratio is given on the page.
corrections.workload: Bulk load + range/nearest queries, and insert/erase/reinsert + range queries, on point and box keys (2D/3D, float/double) over synthetic sets (uniform, skewed, clusters, polygon, parcels) and real ESRI-shapefile/OBJ datasets, 10^2 to 10^6 elements
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark; CPU model and compiler flags not stated in README (a commit message mentions AVX2 + LTO enabled for MSVC); raw results live in ikolev21/ikolev21.github.io (not opened). Same README reports nanoflann faster on point nearest queries up to 10^5, GEOS faster on the Polygon box dataset, tidwall on 2D box sets around 10^4-10^5. Repo has 0 stars.

notes: Claims check out against the current README; license BSL-1.0 confirmed from LICENSE.txt; last commit 2026-09-06 from commits page.

tier_reason: Vendor blog with first-party numbers vs CGAL, Manifold, Blender on an Apple M5 with min-of-10 methodology, but the blog says benchmark source code 'will be opened publicly later' and compiler/flags are not stated.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Nefertiti (2M triangles) union: 47x faster than CGAL, 2.9x faster than Manifold, 153x faster than Blender; on the dental scan CGAL hangs while MeshLib finishes in ~44 ms
corrections.license: Proprietary non-commercial/educational license (AMV Consulting, LLC); commercial license sold separately
corrections.caveats: Vendor blog from the company selling the product; benchmark source code not yet public (inputs, runners' outputs and timing JSON on a SharePoint link); compiler and flags not stated; default threading (multi-threaded). Source-available, non-commercial license: must not be copied. 47x/153x gains with unstated flags.

notes: License file is a non-commercial trial/education agreement, so usability 'reference' stands. Last commit read from the commits page.

tier_reason: README section 3.2 shows first-party charts and states '~50% time saving with respect to the original flann implementation'; perf-tests/ code is public but CPU model, compiler and flags are not stated.

corrections.caveats: Baseline FLANN is not in the category list; README numbers are charts without stated CPU/compiler/flags (reproduction code in perf-tests/); nanoflann is a code-level fork of FLANN (not a GitHub fork); latest release 1.14.0 (2026-09-25); the Boost.Geometry comparison comes only from the GeoToolbox README, where nanoflann wins point nearest queries up to 10^5 elements and uses the least memory.

notes: COPYING text is the 2-clause BSD license, so BSD-2-Clause is confirmed. Benchmark code lives at https://github.com/jlblancoc/nanoflann/tree/master/perf-tests (linked from README, not opened).
